newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Thousands protest in Serbia ahead of OSCE report.
newsitem.headline: Thousands protest in Serbia ahead of OSCE report.

text.p: Thousands of demonstrators for and against President Milosevic took to the streets of Serbia on Sunday ahead of an OSCE verdict on alleged election fraud which the opposition believes will be in its favour.
A mission from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) investigating Serbia's election fraud crisis wound up its work in Belgrade on Saturday.
Mission head Felipe Gonzalez, the former Spanish prime minister, has said he will make recommendations within a week.

The Zajedno coalition of opposition parties says it has proved to the OSCE that it was cheated of victory in Belgrade and 14 other towns in local elections -- the spark for huge street demonstrations against Milosevic for the past 35 days.

Opposition sources said the OSCE persuaded Milosevic to surrender the towns, including Belgrade, but that he would exercise his right to call a fresh poll early in 1997 to try to recover them for his ruling socialist party (SPS).
An American member of the OSCE team, Max Kampelman, said the evidence of election fraud "seems to be impressive."

Zajedno leader Vojin Dimitrijevic said "contrary to prior arrangement, President Milosevic declined to receive Gonzalez at the end of the visit, indicating that the authorities do not like the line the mission is pursuing."
Some 80,000 opposition supporters demonstrated in Belgrade on Sunday in the almost freezing cold.
In the southern Serbian town of Smederevo, the socialists managed to assemble 1,500 people in a counter-demonstration meant to prove Milosevic still had widespread support.
Zajedno said the socialists were planning to hold "final" demonstrations in Belgrade in support of Milosevic on Tuesday.
It said some 1,000 buses and trains will be used to transport Milosevic supporters into the capital. The SPS was paying for the fuel and daily allowances, Zajedno said.

"Do not be angry at those poor people chain-ganged for the event. They too will soon realise they have been robbed of their money and dignity by the dictator," Vesna Pesic, another Zajedno leader referring to Milosevic, told the Belgrade rally.

But a threatened blockade of all major roads as of Monday by Serbian farmers demanding the government pay back its dues for the summer crop and cut taxes, could hamper SPS plans to bus people into Belgrade by the thousands.
Diplomats fear mounting hatred and the proximity of the two rival groups could easily spark violence both Zajedno leaders and Milosevic have promised to avoid.

The state media, run by socialist hardliners reported to be increasingly independent from Milosevic, has increased its campaign against the opposition, calling them traitors to the Serbian cause and servants of the West.
Zajedno accused the SPS of "continuing its anti-American and anti-European campaign, trying again to create an atmosphere of enmity and chauvinism against the whole world."
Zajedno announced it will establish its own Radio and Television network "illegally if need be".
In another development, Zajedno leader Zoran Djindjic said Serbia's central government has cut municipal budget funding to cities and towns where opposition forces recently won.

"This is a crime to punish the citizens who voted for the opposition. It's an assault on the elementary civic right -- freedom of choice...this regime has lost its head, its compass, and is behaving like an elephant in a glass shop."

The opposition leader appeared at a Sunday meeting of the newly-founded Association of Free Cities and Municipalities, a collection of other opposition figures who, like himself, won local elections but have been barred from taking power.
Zajedno accused police of intimidating the population of smaller towns to stop them demonstrating after Vranje activist Goran Krstic was arrested and beaten on Thursday.
Other arrests were reported in Zajecar, Kraljevo. On Sunday the police arrested three opposition supporters only because they jeered at the pro-Milosevic rally in Smederevo.
